hook.line: When the family's future is on the line, everyone around you has advice, and you will want to give some back. Spanish has a neat way to say "I recommend that you..." and "I'm asking you to...".
hook.es: Te recomiendo que hables con un abogado.
hook.en: I recommend that you talk to a lawyer.

examples.es: Te recomiendo que hables con un abogado.
examples.en: I recommend that you talk to a lawyer. (to a friend)
I'm asking him to listen to me.

examples.es: Les aconsejo que no firmen nada.
examples.en: I advise you not to sign anything. (to a group)

examples.es: Vale te pide que cocines hoy.
examples.en: Vale is asking you to cook today. (to a friend)

examples.es: No te recomiendo que vendas el café.
examples.en: I don't recommend that you sell the café. (to a friend)
What do you recommend that I order? (to a friend)

rule:
To tell someone what you advise or ask of them, use three pieces:

*Te recomiendo* + *que* + a new verb form.

The person you are advising comes first (*te*, *le*, *les*, *me*). Then the advice verb: *recomiendo*, *pido*, *aconsejo*, *sugiero*. Then *que*. The verb after *que* is for the other person's action, and it changes its ending to the "asking" form.

For *-ar* verbs the ending switches to *-e*: *hablas* becomes *hables*. For *-er* and *-ir* verbs it switches to *-a*: *comes* becomes *comas*, *escribes* becomes *escribas*.

English says "I recommend that you talk" or just "I'd talk to...". Spanish always keeps *que* and the changed ending.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after verbs of influence: you are trying to influence what someone else does.

readAndPick.es: Te recomiendo que hables con un abogado.
options: I recommend that you talk to a lawyer.
I recommend that he talks to a lawyer.
You recommend that I talk to a lawyer.
He asks me to listen.
I ask him to listen to me.
I ask you to listen to him.

readAndPick.es: Les aconsejo que no firmen nada.
options: I advise you all not to sign anything.
They advise me not to sign anything.
I advise you all to sign everything.

readAndPick.es: Vale te pide que cocines hoy.
options: Vale asks me to cook today.
You ask Vale to cook today.
Vale asks you to cook today.

readAndPick.es: No te recomiendo que vendas el café.
options: I recommend that you sell the café.
I don't recommend that you sell the café.
I don't recommend that he sells the café.
What do I recommend that you order?
What do you recommend that I order?
What do you recommend that she orders?
I ask you to help me.
You ask me to help you.
I ask him to help me.

readAndPick.es: Mariana te recomienda que pruebes el tinto.
options: Mariana recommends that you try the black coffee.
You recommend that Mariana tries the black coffee.
Mariana recommends that I try the black coffee.

options: We ask them to write a plan.
They ask us to write a plan.
They ask us to read a plan.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *hablas* or *hables* and type the whole sentence: *Te recomiendo que ___ con un abogado.*
yourTurn.answer: Te recomiendo que hables con un abogado.
yourTurn.why: After *te recomiendo que*, an *-ar* verb takes *-es* instead of *-as*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *comes* or *comas* and type the whole sentence: *Te recomiendo que ___ algo.*
Type in Spanish: I'm asking him to listen to me.
accept: Yo le pido que me escuche.
yourTurn.why: *Le* is the person you ask, and *escuche* is the changed ending for *él*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I ask you to help me.
accept: Yo te pido que me ayudes.
yourTurn.why: *Te* for the friend, *que*, then *ayudes*, the changed form of *ayudas*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: I recommend that you sleep more.
accept: Yo te recomiendo que duermas más.
yourTurn.why: *Dormir* changes in the middle (*duermes*) and the ending switches to *-as*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Te recomiendo que vendas el café.* Say: I don't recommend that you sell the café. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: No te recomiendo que vendas el café.
accept: Yo no te recomiendo que vendas el café.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* in front of the whole advice verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a group: I advise you not to sign anything.
yourTurn.answer: Les aconsejo que no firmen nada.
accept: Yo les aconsejo que no firmen nada.
yourTurn.why: *Les* for a group, and *no* goes right before the changed verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: What do you recommend that I order?
yourTurn.why: *Me* is the person getting the advice, and *pida* is the changed form of *pido*.

pitfalls.wrong: Te recomiendo que hablas con un abogado.
pitfalls.right: Te recomiendo que hables con un abogado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After advice or a request, the verb after *que* changes its ending: *hables*, not *hablas*.

pitfalls.wrong: Te recomiendo que hables a un abogado.
pitfalls.right: Te recomiendo que hables con un abogado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. To talk to someone, Spanish says *hablar con*.

pitfalls.wrong: Te pido que tú me ayudes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Te* already says who is doing the helping, so *tú* is not needed.
Almost. Spanish keeps *que* here, even though English can drop "that".

personal: Tell a friend one thing you recommend that they do this week, starting with *Te recomiendo que*.
